text: The Davao City Fire District Special Rescue Force DCFD-SRF brings Swift Water Search and Rescue Training to Bureau of Fire Protection Central Luzon because preparedness knows no distance Under the leadership of FCSUPT RIZALDE M CASTRO Regional Director and under the direct supervision of District Fire Marshal FSUPT DONALD R CONCEPCION headed by FSINSP REOMAR C BUCAO the Davao City Fire District Special Rescue Force DCFD-SRF successfully conducted the Swift Water Search and Rescue Training for personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection Central Luzon The training equipped participants with essential knowledge techniques and practical skills in Swift Water Search and Rescue SWSAR enhancing their preparedness and operational capability in responding to emergencies involving floods swift currents and other water-related incidents The activity was further strengthened through the participation of Disaster Risk Reduction and Management DRRM personnel from the City of Palayan and the Municipality of Talavera whose involvement underscores the importance of inter-agency cooperation and community-based preparedness in disaster response and rescue operations The Davao City Fire District Special Rescue Force extends its sincere appreciation to FSSUPT BERNARD T ROSETE DSC Acting Regional Director BFP Region 3 for the support and leadership extended toward the successful conduct of this capability-building initiative Likewise heartfelt appreciation is extended to the Nueva Ecija Provincial Office BFP R3 for its invaluable cooperation and support which contributed significantly to the successful conduct of this training We sincerely acknowledge the Provincial Office and all its personnel whose dedication and active participation helped make this important training initiative a success From Davao City to Central Luzon this training serves as a reminder that preparedness knows no distance Through knowledge-sharing skills development and strengthened inter-regional cooperation we continue to build a more capable and responsive firefighting and rescue force Congratulations to all the participants and training team for the successful completion of As communities continue to recover from widespread flooding caused by the southwest monsoon habagat Senator Christopher Bong Go urged the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH to expedite the construction and completion of permanent evacuation centers nationwide Heavy monsoon rains recently inundated several areas across Luzon with provinces such as Pampanga among the severely affected areas prompting government rescue operations in Central Luzon During the Senate deliberations on the DPWH's proposed 2027 budget on September 25 Go emphasized that recurring flooding highlights the urgent need for safe and dedicated evacuation shelters instead of temporary facilities such as schools and gyms Ako mismo pinupuntahan ko talaga yan Pampanga Bulacan naaawa talaga ako sa Pilipino Go said recalling the difficult conditions he personally witnessed in submerged communities Tulungan n'yo naman po sila Kayo po ang nandiyan sa executive department pakiuna na lang po na ma-address itong problema ng flooding po Kawawa talaga At yung iba po naiiwan sa mga evacuation centers Yung iba eskwelahan gym Hindi sila kumportable yung iba walang maayos na sanitation he added Go serves as the principal author and co-sponsor of Republic Act No 12076 or the Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act which was enacted in December 2024 and mandates the establishment of evacuation centers in every city and municipality Addressing DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon Go urged the agency to prioritize the construction of these facilities amid the country's frequent experience of typhoons earthquakes and seasonal flooding Sana po mabigyan n'yo po ito ng prayoridad itong mga evacuation centers Mapapakinabangan po ito ng mga kababayan natin Batas na po ito Go asserted He also called on the DPWH to review existing projects funded under the 2025 and 2026 budgets to ensure that near-complete structures are completed without further delay In response Secretary Dizon reported that 464 of the 492 Ligtas Pinoy evacuation center projects had been completed as of late August while 24 remained under construction He added that approximately PHP 3.06 billion had been programmed for 2027 for the construction of two evacuation centers per region We will prioritize Mr Chairman You have our assurance po Dizon assured the Senate panel Mr Malasakit Bisyo Ang Mag Serbisyo Senator Bong Go

As extreme weather severe flooding and crippling traffic continue to impact Metro Manila it becomes clear that single-purpose infrastructure is no longer enough We need multi-functional climate-resilient solutions designed for long-term survival In 1989 Arch Felino Jun Palafox Jr proposed a bold vision to complete the C 10 regional loop a tunnel interconnecting Bataan and Cavite Designed as a bridge and multi-tier underwater megastructure this concept serves a dual purpose 1 Transport and Connectivity Inspired by global best practices it links Central Luzon and Calabarzon directly-accommodating trains buses cars active mobility and utilities while bypassing the heavily congested roads of Metro Manila 2 Flood Management and Coastal Protection Similar to Malaysia's SMART Tunnel the infrastructure doubles as a massive flood control spillway during severe typhoons while acting as a natural wave breaker against storm surges By decentralizing Metro Manila and investing in dual-purpose infrastructure we can build a connected climate-resilient Philippines that protects both lives and livelihoods The best time to act was 37 years ago the second best time is today Pro Deo Patria et Terra PALAFOX

DAVAO FLOODING AND THE DUTERTES A Balanced Assessment AN HONEST STARTING POINT Flooding in Davao is a legitimate concern that deserves serious attention Some of the criticisms are grounded in real events including a genuine solid-waste crisis that cost lives this year At the same time much of the social-media commentary exaggerates the problem blurs who's actually responsible and paints this as a uniquely Duterte-family failure A fair assessment holds both things at once real gaps and a national context that critics conveniently leave out NATIONAL REALITY CHECK Flood control is a hard problem everywhere in the Philippines Outdated drainage garbage-choked waterways siltation and urbanization that outpaced 1970s-era infrastructure overwhelm every major city in heavy rain No LGU not Manila not Cebu not Davao has a flood-free rainy season Anyone claiming otherwise about any city is selling something Davao carries the same systemic pressures as its peers but has put more visible work into the problem than most WHAT HAS BEEN DELIVERED Multiple drainage and flood-control projects since 2022 prioritized in high-risk districts including river rehabilitation on the Matina Bunawan and Davao River systems Seven DPWH pumping stations already operating across the city Jerome Mamay Agdao Marginal-to-Magsaysay Ponce Roxas ext Mabini ext plus two more in Laverna with a third proposed City-funded drainage rehabilitation including PHP 35 million for the CSC road drainage and PHP 40 million for the Kabacan creek in Ecoland Residents in upgraded zones report noticeably faster water recession after heavy downpours compared to before these projects this is anecdotal rather than a published city metric but it's a consistent report worth taking seriously rather than dismissing Rodrigo Duterte's earlier line-item vetoes of questionable DPWH insertions reflected a genuine stance against pork-barrel-style spending which matters when we're talking about whether flood money gets spent honestly These are real verifiable steps not just promises WHERE THE RECORD IS GENUINELY WEAK AND NEEDS TO BE SAID PLAINLY This is the part critics will hammer so let's not soften it on May 20 2026 a portion of the New Carmen sanitary landfill collapsed after days of heavy rain killing at least one person and leaving others missing on top of injuries and displaced families DENR suspended the landfill days later cited multiple violations of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act and permanently closed the old site in June That is not a maintenance footnote it was a fatal disaster and it happened on this administration's watch Pretending otherwise would be dishonest BEYOND THAT INCIDENT THE UNDERLYING PROBLEMS ARE REAL AND LONGSTANDING The landfill was already operating well past design capacity for years before it collapsed waste disposal roughly doubled from 2010 levels by 2025 and this was a known documented problem not a surprise Drainage systems in several barangays have not received consistent desilting Uncollected and improperly dumped garbage continues to clog canals and drainage inlets citywide and enforcement against illegal dumping and drainage encroachment remains inconsistent The new landfill and expansion projects were already underway before the collapse which shows the problem was recognized but recognizing a problem is not the same as having fixed it in time Full transparency on the landfill collapse investigation and a public accounting of why the old site was allowed to run so far past capacity is the least residents deserve COMPARATIVE PERSPECTIVE None of this erases the comparison that matters how does Davao stack up against LGUs facing the same pressures On project delivery and the resources actually put toward flood mitigation pumping stations river rehabilitation drainage funding Davao has more to point to than many cities of similar size and budget That doesn't make Davao's flooding acceptable It means the uniquely incompetent Duterte fiefdom narrative pushed on social media doesn't survive contact with what other LGUs are or aren't doing with comparable resources KEY CLARIFICATIONS The PHP 51 billion figure widely cited for Rep Paolo Duterte's district 2020-2022 is routinely presented online as if it were all flood-control spending It wasn't DPWH-Davao itself has clarified the figure later refined to PHP 49.8 billion covered the district's entire infrastructure portfolio roads bridges multipurpose buildings and major projects like the Davao Coastal Road and Bypass Road DPWH's own breakdown puts the flood-control share at roughly PHP 9 billion a fraction of the total Treating the full PHP 51B as a flood-control budget then pointing at continued flooding as proof the money didn't work is a category error not an accountability finding That said a real question remains open and shouldn't be waved away

Laguna de Bay the largest lake in the Philippines is facing serious environmental challenges as pollution sediment accumulation and rapid urban development continue to place pressure on its ecosystem In August 2025 Biñan City Representative Walfredo Arman Dimaguila Jr warned that the lake could eventually become the country's largest septic tank if its deteriorating condition is not addressed His statement highlighted concerns about untreated wastewater industrial pollutants accumulated sediments and recurring flooding affecting communities surrounding the lake Covering approximately 900 square kilometers Laguna de Bay plays an important role in fisheries livelihoods water supply and flood regulation across Laguna Rizal and parts of Metro Manila However the lawmaker's description was a warning about environmental deterioration rather than a literal assessment of the lake's water quality Scientific assessments have identified several interconnected threats to Laguna de Bay including nutrient pollution siltation and eutrophication a process in which excessive nutrients stimulate algal growth and can contribute to oxygen depletion Wastewater from households industrial activities agricultural runoff and improper waste disposal can introduce organic matter nutrients microorganisms and other contaminants into the lake and its tributaries According to historical monitoring information from the Laguna Lake Development Authority LLDA domestic sources have contributed substantially to the lake's organic pollution load Excessive nutrients can encourage algal blooms while the decomposition of organic matter may reduce dissolved oxygen concentrations potentially harming fish and other aquatic organisms Sediment accumulation can also affect aquatic habitats and water movement although the extent to which it reduces floodwater storage requires updated measurements and hydrological assessment These environmental pressures are particularly concerning because many lakeshore communities depend on the lake for food income and other essential services In October 2026 Laguna lawmakers renewed calls for coordinated flood management through House Resolution No 906 which seeks an integrated approach involving updated lake surveys targeted dredging watershed rehabilitation erosion control and technical evaluation of flood mitigation infrastructure However scientists and environmental planners emphasize that dredging alone cannot solve water pollution especially when untreated wastewater and other contaminants continue entering the lake Effective rehabilitation requires improved sewerage and wastewater treatment stricter enforcement of environmental regulations responsible industrial waste management restoration of surrounding watersheds and continuous scientific monitoring Large-scale dredging proposals must also undergo careful environmental and engineering evaluation to determine their potential benefits costs and ecological impacts Protecting Laguna de Bay is not simply about preventing floods or removing accumulated sediments It is about safeguarding an essential freshwater ecosystem supporting fishing communities protecting public health and ensuring that future generations can continue to benefit from one of the Philippines most important natural resources Science Department Laguna De Bay FLASHFLOOD EMERGENCY in Urban areas Immediate Action Stay Put and Signal If you are already stranded-whether on a roof in a car or on high ground-your primary goal is to wait for help Do not attempt to travel through the floodwaters 1 Get to the Highest and Safest Point In a Building Move immediately to the highest accessible floor AVOID a closed attic If the water continues to rise you could become trapped without a way to escape Only go onto the roof if absolutely necessary If you do have a way to break through like an axe or shovel if accessible to prevent being trapped in an enclosed attic space In a Vehicle Do NOT drive through any floodwater If your vehicle is surrounded by rapidly moving water Stay in the vehicle unless the water is rising inside If water is rising inside the vehicle get out immediately and climb onto the roof If you can try to roll down windows early to equalize pressure and make the car less buoyant/more stable then climb out Outside on High Ground Stay there Do not attempt to cross or walk through any moving water 2 Signal for Help Rescuers must be able to see you especially when the storm makes visibility low Visibility Use brightly colored clothing or fabric red orange or reflective material and wave it when you hear a helicopter or see a boat Sound Use a whistle which can carry sound better than screaming or bang on a metal object in a set pattern like three short bangs Light Use a flashlight or the light on your phone to flash an SOS signal three short three long three short flashes at night or toward a distant search team Communication If you have a working mobile phone call emergency services Survival and Safety While Stranded 3 Manage the Hazards of the Water Floodwater is extremely dangerous often called black water Contamination Assume all floodwater is contaminated with sewage chemicals sharp debris broken glass metal and potential biological hazards Electrocution Stay clear of downed power lines Floodwater can become electrically charged Do not touch any electrical equipment if you are wet or standing in water Debris and Animals Watch out for floating debris that can injure you Snakes insects and other displaced animals may also be seeking refuge on your elevated spot 4 Conserve Resources If you have your emergency kit with you Water Ration drinking water carefully If you have absolutely no safe drinking water you may need to use rainwater collection but purification methods should be used if possible Never drink floodwater Power Keep your phone powered off or in airplane mode unless actively communicating with rescuers or checking for official alerts Food Ration non-perishable food items 5 Stay Alert and Monitor Conditions Official Alerts Listen to a battery-powered or hand-crank radio for official announcements evacuation orders or changes in the storm path Follow instructions from local emergency management immediately Structural Integrity If you are in a building be alert for shifting noises cracks or signs of structural stress especially if the wind and water are still severe Key Advice to Remember Do Not Enter Moving Water Just 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet Do Not Attempt to Swim to Safety The current hidden debris and contamination make this a last resort Stay Warm and Dry If possible use blankets or dry clothes from your emergency bag to prevent hypothermia which can happen even in warm climates due to wind and rain Your single best defense now is to remain where you are the highest point stay visible and wait for official rescue teams

through the Pampanga River Basin Flood Forecasting and Warning Center PRBFFWC conducted a training-workshop on Flood Forecasting and Warning System to strengthen flood forecasting warning operations and coordination among partner agencies in the Pampanga River Basin on October 13-16 2026 Held at the Social Action Center of Pampanga SACOP Ephata in Barangay Maimpis the activity focused on proving deeper understanding on river basin characteristics stream gaging flood forecasting and improving the clarity timeliness and dissemination of flood warnings to local government units and at-risk communities It also emphasized inter-agency coordination and the proper operation and maintenance of monitoring equipment to ensure reliable data for flood forecasting Participants discussed rainfall and river monitoring flood forecasting and procedures for issuing flood advisories and bulletins Sessions also covered how watershed characteristics influence flooding how floodwaters move through river systems and how post-flood assessments can inform future operations To complement the discussions participants conducted field exercises along the Pampanga River in San Luis Pampanga They surveyed the river's cross-section observed water levels measured flow velocity and calculated the volume of water flowing through the river-providing hands-on experience in collecting and interpreting data used in flood forecasting A workshop session titled From Warning to Action Partner Agencies Flood Response Protocol focused on coordinating agency responses to flood warnings Participants also shared feedback and recommendations on the center's flood advisories bulletins and visual presentation of information and identified opportunities for further collaboration Joining PRBFFWC personnel were representatives from the Office of Civil Defense-Region III Department of Science and Technology-Region III Mines and Geosciences Bureau-Region III National Irrigation Administration-Upper Pampanga River Integrated Irrigation Systems and the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices of Pampanga and Bulacan Participants from other agencies also DAVAO THE FLOOD CAPITAL BUT PERHAPS NOT FOR THE REASON YOU THINK They say Davao is the Flood Capital of the Philippines Well if someone insists on giving us that crown perhaps we should wear it proudly-but let's first ask a simple question What exactly is overflowing Yes Davao experiences floods We have rivers that swell after relentless rain low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools That is a real problem It deserves real solutions-not political theater But if we are going to compare cities perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan During the severe southwest monsoon flooding in July 2025 for example the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across Metro Manila within a single day So before anyone points a finger at Davao perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city Water does not check political affiliations before it rises Rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours And rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches But here's where I see Davao differently Because there is another kind of flooding happening here-one that doesn't destroy homes close roads or leave mud behind Davao floods with culture Walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of Mindanao Indigenous traditions migrant communities different languages cuisines beliefs stories and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry Ask someone where they came from and you may discover an entire story behind the answer Then inevitably there's food Because in Davao you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian This variety is sweeter No that one has better texture You haven't tried the best one yet Suddenly what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian No registration fee required But perhaps Davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture It is warmth There is a quiet generosity in the character of many Dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure You can arrive as a stranger and before long someone may already be telling you where to eat what places to visit which shortcut to take-and most importantly which road to avoid when traffic is terrible That's not just hospitality That's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory And then there is Davao's natural beauty The sea Samal Mount Apo The forests The farms The rivers The mountains The wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies Davao is also changing Businesses are arriving Buildings are rising Infrastructure is expanding Communities are growing People continue to come-not only because they are looking for jobs but because they are looking for possibilities Some arrive carrying résumés Others arrive carrying business plans Some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream And somewhere along the way many discover something unexpected They don't merely live in Davao They become part of it That perhaps is the real story A city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it It should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems Davao is not perfect We have traffic We have growing pains We have environmental concerns We have infrastructure challenges We have political disagreements And of course we have social-media experts who can apparently repair the entire country using nothing but a smartphone and a Facebook account But beneath all the noise is something far more difficult to construct Character You can build a highway You can build skyscrapers You can build malls bridges offices and massive developments You can even build a spectacular roundabout that everyone will complain about for months But you cannot manufacture belonging You cannot pour it into concrete You cannot buy it from a catalog It has to grow And Davao has grown through people People from different places came here They planted roots They built families They opened businesses They raised children They created communities And little by little their individual stories became part of the larger story of the city For the past 15 years I text: PHP 47 M Flood Control Project in Laoag Collapses Ties Emerge Between Contractor Linked to Davao Lawmaker and Sandro Marcos Office A newly built flood control structure along Padsan River in Barangay Gabu Laoag City a project worth PHP 47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 General Appropriations Act GAA has collapsed JUST MONTHS after its reported completion sparking fresh outrage over the alleged flood-control mafia operating in Congress Photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked dislodged and washed into the river exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion The project billboard names RA Pahati Construction and Supply Inc as the contractor under the DPWH Ilocos Norte First District Engineering Office with a target completion date of October 4 2024 RA Pahati Construction is reportedly owned by the family of Rep Jhong Ceniza of Pantukan Davao de Oro a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles Sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that RA Pahati has become a favored builder for Rep Sandro Marcos the Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative allegedly with some help from his chief of staff said to be a relative of Rep Ceniza's wife Residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks Infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction adequate riprap foundation and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction all of which appear deficient in the broken sections The collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a cash cow for certain districts RA Pahati controlled by the Ceniza family has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across Luzon and Mindanao despite originating from Davao de Oro In Ilocos Norte whispers persist that Rep Sandro Marcos chief of staff reportedly related by marriage to the Cenizas has been instrumental in channeling projects to RA Pahati bypassing stricter vetting Political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive DPWH flood control budgets The incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide long suspected to be overpriced poorly built and politically manipulated In Congress several lawmakers particularly from Mindanao have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals Observers warn that this Laoag project could become a flashpoint especially since it sits in the home turf of the President's son who is expected to champion good governance but now faces scrutiny over his district's infrastructure spending

a traffic reliever-it's a massive multi-purpose flood control and coastal protection project Here's how it plays a vital role in flood resilience and urban development 1 Storm-Surge Barrier and Coastal Defense Designed as a coastal bypass the project doubles as a breakwater and shore protection system defending against sea wave actions storm surges and coastal erosion It incorporates hexapods seawalls grouted riprap and other shoreline defenses to reduce wave impact-a thoughtfully engineered coastline safeguard 2 Integrated Roadway and Public Spaces The 4 lane highway with asphalt pavement bike lanes pedestrian sidewalks and a 25.54 meter full-width design serves mobility recreation and safety purposes Includes linear parks esplanades and promenades perfect for walking jogging or biking-offering both functional and leisure value 3 Strategic Flood Resilience The elevated embankmented structure approx 6.5 meters on average complete with drainage frameworks helps mitigate flooding from coastal surges and heavy rains Though technically it doesn't span rivers its design contributes indirectly to reducing flood impact in adjacent areas-especially during storm surges 4 Complementing River Flood Control Efforts Meanwhile along the Davao River DPWH is reinforcing revetment walls in Baranguay Mandug with structural sheet piles concrete capping and embankment fortification to control river flooding These efforts are nearing 90-94 percent completion and are slated for wrap-up by Q4 2025 These projects operate synergistically-coastal road handling storm surge while river revetment mitigates overflow inland 5 Timeline and Scale The 17.8 km coastal road also called the Coastal Bypass Road began in 2017 and is rolling out in phases with major segments When the Waters Rise in Davao City So Do the Online Critics Following the heavy rains brought by the Habagat and recent weather systems on July 24 2026 several neighborhoods across Davao City once again faced rising floodwaters From Mandug and Tugbok down to low-lying areas like Bangkal Matina and Talomo families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels moving to higher ground or waiting for emergency teams And like clockwork as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media the comments section lit up with the usual outrage political potshots and online bashing Where did the billions go Why hasn't the city solved flooding yet It is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes But using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science geography and non-stop work happening on the ground Here is the perspective every Dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear 1 You Cannot Out-Engineer a Catch Basin No politician regardless of their party and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography Davao City sits beside major river systems Davao Talomo Matina Lipadas Bunawan and Lasang flowing straight into the gulf Key areas like Bago Gallera Talomo Proper Ulas Bangkal and Matina are natural catch basins When continuous rains hit the highlands upstream millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations Add a high tide at the coast and the ocean acts like a giant dam preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea Dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean 2 Nature Remembers Its Original Shape Parts of Boulevard Bucana Agdao and Sta Ana were historically mudflats swamps and coastal wetlands Humans can pave over these landscapes with roads subdivisions and concrete structures but when extreme rainfall happens water simply reclaims its natural pathways With climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year This is a regional and global environmental challenge not an isolated municipal flaw 3 Where Did the Funds Go Look at the Defense Systems in Place Critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear But flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling it's built to slow down water protect riverbanks and buy critical time Pumping Stations and Retarding Basins Built in notorious bottlenecks like Sasa and La Verna to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers Revetment Walls and Dikes Miles of concrete dikes line the Matina Talomo and Davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges Early Warning and River Monitoring The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office CDRRMO operates automated sensors and live HD monitoring cameras along all six major river channels allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks 4 While Keyboard Warriors Bash Responders Are Out in the Dark While critics type away in dry rooms hundreds of frontline responders from the CDRRMO BFP Davao Light urban search and rescue SAR units and barangay disaster teams are out in waist-deep water executing rescue operations clearing clogged channels and moving stranded families to safety Good governance in a coastal river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities it's measured by preparedness quick response and zero casualties The fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system Bashing Davao City during a flood won't lower the tide and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain Instead of tearing each other down let's focus on what actually keeps us safe community preparedness and cooperation When the CDRRMO issues a Code Red or sounds the warning siren do not wait Follow But why blame President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr for a flood-control problem that his administration itself exposed During his Fourth State of the Nation Address on July 28 2025 President Marcos publicly revealed the alarming irregularities in flood-control projects and ordered their inspection and verification Investigations subsequently uncovered projects allegedly reported as completed but found to be nonexistent defective improperly located or below required standards-some dating back to 2016 during the previous administration The issue is not simply how much money was appropriated but whether Filipinos actually received the infrastructure they paid for Billions of pesos cannot simply disappear while projects exist only on paper If public officials or contractors misused government funds they must be held accountable under Article XI Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution which declares that public office is a public trust and under Republic Act No 3019 the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act Of course the Marcos administration must also be held accountable for projects undertaken during its own term No administration should be above scrutiny But it is unfair to automatically blame the incumbent president for every consequence of decades of inadequate or allegedly anomalous infrastructure A problem inherited for years cannot be corrected overnight Investigating questionable projects identifying those responsible recovering public funds prosecuting offenders and rebuilding failed infrastructure take time If corruption occurred under the previous administration those responsible should answer for it If corruption occurred under the present administration those responsible should likewise face the law The question should therefore not be Why blame PBBM Nor should it be Why blame Duterte The real question is Who received the people's money who failed to deliver what was promised and who should be held accountable Let the evidence text: DAVAO'S FLOOD MAP EXPLAINED Why Different Neighborhoods Face Different Flood Risks When heavy rains hit Davao City why do some neighborhoods experience sudden flash floods that recede in a few hours while others remain submerged under standing water for days It all comes down to catchment hydrology The master plan developed by the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH and the Japan International Cooperation Agency JICA covers 2,200 square kilometers divided into three main river basins Because each catchment has a unique shape slope and size each one poses a completely different flood threat to specific Davao neighborhoods 1 Davao River Basin 1,755 km2 Massive Volume and Standing Water Neighborhoods Affected Waan Tigatto Ma-a Barangay 19 Barangay 8 and Bucana What Happens Here This is the largest river system in the area Because its catchment extends deep into the northern mountain ranges it collects enormous volumes of rainwater Even when it isn't raining in the downtown area heavy rainfall up in the mountains eventually travels downstream into the city The Engineering Reality Because the basin is so large there is a time delay before the main wave of water reaches the city As the river passes through tight natural bends near Tigatto and Ma-a the channel gets squeezed forcing water over the banks Worse when peak river flows meet high tides at the river mouth in Bucana the seawater acts like a natural dam This creates a severe backwater effect that traps floodwaters inland causing deep slow-draining pools that cover over 480 hectares and affect 43,000 residents 2 Matina River Basin 70 km2 Rapid Flash Floods and Highway Bottlenecks Neighborhoods Affected Matina Pangi Gravahan GSIS Subdivision and Matina Crossing What Happens Here Unlike the Davao River Matina suffers from sudden high-speed flash floods with very little warning time The Engineering Reality This basin is relatively small steep and heavily built-up with concrete and asphalt Because rainwater cannot soak into the ground it immediately rushes straight into the river channel Narrow bridge openings-such as the crossing along McArthur Highway-act like narrow bottlenecks When high-volume runoff reaches these tight spots the water backs up rapidly and spills sideways over the banks directly into nearby residential subdivisions 3 Talomo River Basin 204 km2 Raging Currents and Riverbank Collapse Neighborhoods Affected Talomo Proper Tugbok and communities along the Talomo Riverbanks What Happens Here While Talomo does not usually create broad standing lakes like the Davao River its waters move at extremely high speeds as they surge down from the slopes of Mount Apo The Engineering Reality The steep drop in elevation gives the rushing water tremendous kinetic energy Instead of long-term standing pools the main danger here is high-velocity water scraping against the riverbed and riverbanks This severe erosion tears away the surrounding land threatens bridge piers and causes steep riverbanks to collapse along the Talomo-Tugbok corridor 4 The Missing Gaps Intermediate Basins and Urban Creeks Neighborhoods Affected Toril Lipadas River Bunawan and Lasang Bunawan/Licanan Rivers and Agdao Bajada and Buhangin Urban Creek Networks The Planning Limitation On master plan maps you might notice uncolored spaces between the three big basins In nature land is continuous-every square meter belongs to a catchment The JICA study intentionally focused its scope on the three largest high-volume river mains omitting these smaller intermediate catchments Why They Still Matter These smaller watersheds carry severe flood risk For instance the Lipadas River in Toril causes rapid flash evacuations the Bunawan River frequently submerges portions of the Davao-Agusan Highway and dense urban creek networks in Agdao and Buhangin overflow quickly during short thunderstorms because over 95 percent of the city's natural urban wetlands have been paved over Comprehensive city drainage requires addressing these omitted gaps alongside the main rivers The Takeaway Whether it's standing water along the Davao River flash flooding in Matina riverbank erosion in Talomo or creek overflow in Agdao and Toril any effective flood strategy must treat all catchments as interconnected systems DAVAO FLOOD CONTROL SERIES 4 PART DEEP DIVE Read the Full Overview Post Here PART 1 text: Barangay sent 3 warning letters before Callawa Bridge 2 collapse PACC says DAVAO CITY The Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission PACC has launched a formal investigation into the collapse of Callawa Bridge 2 after learning that the Barangay Council of Callawa had allegedly sent at least three warning letters to the Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH before the structure gave way last week According to the PACC the letters raised serious concerns over visible cracks on the bridge severe erosion beneath the structure exposed bridge foundations and posts and the possibility that the bridge could collapse during heavy flooding Residents and barangay officials claimed the warnings were repeatedly brought to the attention of authorities but were allegedly never properly acted upon The bridge collapsed on May 18 following continuous heavy rains triggered by the Intertropical Convergence Zone ITCZ and Easterlies disrupting transportation access and affecting residents and motorists in Barangay Callawa and nearby communities During an ocular inspection conducted Friday PACC officials and volunteer engineers observed extensive erosion and scouring along the bridge approaches with large portions of supporting soil already washed away by strong floodwaters PACC Chairman Dr Louie F Ceniza said the incident raises serious concerns about accountability and public safety If prior warnings were indeed raised by the Barangay Council and residents these concerns should have been immediately addressed before the situation escalated into a disaster Ceniza said The people deserve answers The public deserves accountability he added The inspection was conducted in the presence of PACC BOT Member Rev Richie Cubos DPWH Davao City 3rd District Engineering Office Assistant District Engineer Andrew Pangan and volunteer civil engineers from Davao City assisting in the initial technical assessment The collapsed structure forms part of the DPWH Region XI infrastructure project identified as Project ID No 17L00133 covering the concreting widening and improvement of the Buhangin-Tigatto-Mandug-Callawa-Fatima Road including reconstruction of Callawa Bridge The project implemented by DPWH Region XI and undertaken by contractor Premium Megastructures Inc cost P190.7 million and was completed in December 2018 Initial observations by the PACC indicated that the bridge may have lacked sufficient upstream and downstream flood protection measures Investigators said approximately 100 meters of flood control protection on both sides of the bridge could have minimized or prevented the erosion that undermined the structure The PACC also noted the collapse of nearby utility poles due to severe soil erosion and loss of support As part of the probe the commission said it will review approved engineering plans hydraulic and geotechnical studies construction quality control reports inspection and acceptance records maintenance documents and all correspondence submitted by Barangay Callawa including DPWH responses to the reported concerns PACC BOT Member and Spiritual Adviser Bishop Rod Cubos said the incident highlights the consequences of negligence and inaction This incident reminds us that negligence and indifference can lead to suffering danger and hardship within our communities Cubos said The PACC emphasized that findings from the inspection remain subject to further technical validation and documentary review Meanwhile the commission acknowledged the ongoing efforts of the DPWH Davao City 3rd District city's flooding Instead of just building basic concrete walls which easily overflow the Japanese and local engineers designed a massive city-wide system The core of the plan involves digging massive retarding basins giant empty catch-ponds built in the uplands When a storm hits millions of gallons of water would flow into these basins and be held there safely trapping the water before it ever reaches barangays like Ma-a Matina and Talomo It is brilliant it is proven and it is ready But just look at the timeline of how it got stuck in politics Here is the timeline April 2019 THE STUDY Meet the Surigao del Sur Meteorologist Who's Now with DOST-PAGASA Blaise Christian Perez 24 from Tandag City Surigao del Sur is the first graduate of a Bachelor of Science in Meteorology in the province turning his dream into reality The Surigaonon meteorologist studied at Bicol University and graduated in 2025 He now works in the Central Office of DOST-PAGASA Blaise shared with Ato Ni Bai that it took him multiple routes before landing in BS Meteorology BS Meteorology wasn't the most conventional choice and I was very aware of that when I decided to pursue it he said He applied to several universities including Adamson University and University of Southeastern Philippines for a different course but could not pursue it due to the pandemic He enrolled in BS Medical Laboratory Sciences at San Pedro College in Davao but it didn't work for him Blaise admitted that he wasn't fulfilled and struggled to stay motivated He applied again to another school but it did not work out Despite these setbacks he never lost sight of his childhood dream and chose to pursue it From a young age he was fascinated by how weather worked drawing inspiration from educational channels and science books especially about natural disasters His grandmother's encouragement of his interest in science nurtured this curiosity which later guided him back to his original dream despite exploring other paths There was this persistent feeling an instinct I couldn't ignore that I should go back to what I originally wanted So I applied for BS Meteorology at Bicol University which had always been my first choice he recalled According to Blaise meteorology was not just a chosen course it was his return to something that had always been part of him What began as a child's quiet curiosity about rain became a lifelong pursuit of understanding the atmosphere and more importantly using that understanding to serve and protect communities he said Now the Tandaganon meteorologist is working under the Hydrometeorology Division at the Central Office of DOST-PAGASA I'm working as a Project Technical Specialist under AI4RP at DOST-PAGASA primarily as a researcher within the agency So far the experience has been really fulfilling he shared From what once started as curiosity I now get to work on projects that combine meteorology research and even emerging technologies like AI for disaster risk reduction Beyond his research he was able to apply his expertise directly to help his community understand and respond to extreme weather events He proudly shared that he was given an opportunity to speak about the weather in the local language during coordination meetings with the Tandag CDRRMO for Bagyong Tino and Basyang These opportunities reinforced his commitment to giving back to his home province He feels a strong desire to contribute and work back in Surigao del Sur bringing what he has learned to help empower communities I really see the need to strengthen our local DRRM efforts especially in terms of climate resilience and more importantly effective science communication sa atong early warning systems Kitang tanan naka-experience kung unsa ka grabe ang epekto sa mga bagyo especially recently with TS Basyang nga nagdala og grabe nga pagbaha sa atoang probinsya labi na sa Tandag he said He also highlights that education and awareness are crucial and preparedness should be prioritized especially in the community People should be well-informed of PAGASA forecasts including warnings and know what to do before during and after a hazard Hindi man natin mapipigilan ang bagyo o ulan But through preparedness we can save lives ma minusan ang damage and make our communities more resilient he added To those planning to pursue meteorology Blaise shared that they should build a strong foundation in math and physics He advised them to stay curious and explore be patient with themselves and remember that the field is not just about forecasting it is about serving people and communities Padayon lang gyud even if the path feels uncertain or uncommon Dili man siya popular nga course but that doesn't make it any less important if anything mas kinahanglan pa gani siya karon he shared From a curious child in Tandag City to a meteorologist with plans for his home province's disaster preparedness Blaise shows how passion persistence and dedication can
